rv.q: This atmospheric play is good fare for theatergoers who are horror curious but easily spooked.
Without a doubt, this horrifying legend of Dracula will forever be remembered as one of City Lit’s finest productions.
The dramatic irony undergirding the events that befell the Demeter makes for a perfect spooky season treat.
The solid ten-member ensemble...is buoyed by imaginative and well-integrated design work...and Jeremiah Barr's puppetry adds an unusual, eerily effective element to the evocative storytelling.
I can’t be too cross with a show that’s this imaginative, intelligent, and well-acted.
The excellence of the performances outshine the meager script.
This world premiere presentation, directed by Ed Rutherford, is perfect for the Halloween season!
Though the tension is a little lacking, the cast’s performances do show us their descent into madness by the happenings around them.

cn.t: Critics praise this atmospheric adaptation of Dracula's seventh chapter as a moody, macabre horror tale. Timothy Griffin's script and the production's compelling staging of murder and mayhem aboard the doomed Demeter earn strong reviews.
